Subject: Token accounting + baseline pricing (quick answers please)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Before we loop procurement in, two quick technical/pricing clarifications so we can model monthly costs precisely:

1) Token accounting: does Redwood bill hosted API calls on the sum of input + output tokens per call? Specifically: are system role tokens counted as input tokens? And if the model triggers a function/tool call (we use a function wrapper to call an internal DB), are the tokens for the function name/arguments counted as input, output, or both? Also if the tool returns some text that the model then includes in its final response, how is that treated?

2) Rounding/granularity: do you meter fractional tokens or do you round per-call? If we stream responses, is billing done as tokens are emitted or still aggregated per-request? Any per-request minimums we should model?

3) Baseline hosted rate card for forecasting: we need list prices for your common hosted tiers (LLM-small / LLM-medium / LLM-large) for both input and output tokens so we can plug into our cost model. Also please flag if embeddings or retrieval tooling are priced differently.

4) If we sign up with a committed annual spend (ballpark: $250k - $600k), what discount ranges do you typically offer? Procurement is sensitive to how the list price maps to committed pricing.

I attached a short forecast (acme_consume_forecast.xlsx). If you can send a short written explanation I can forward to our procurement team.

Thanks,

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>

Hi — quick authoritative blurb and a numeric example below. Kept it procurement-friendly.

Short explanation (copy/paste friendly):
Redwood bills hosted API usage per API call as the sum of tokens consumed by the request (input side) plus tokens produced by the model (output side). "Input tokens" include any system prompt tokens, user prompt tokens, and any tool/function arguments that are supplied as part of the request payload. "Output tokens" include the tokens returned by the model in its assistant response; if the model invokes a tool and the tool's returned text is subsequently included in the assistant's final message to the client, those tool-return tokens are counted as output tokens (not double-counted). We tokenize client-supplied strings first; token counts are integer-valued—billing is per token with no fractional token billing. Streaming responses are metered as tokens are emitted; there is no additional per-request minimum. Embeddings and other non-chat APIs are billed separately and are not part of the chat token sum.

Worked example (rounded counts):
- System prompt: 24 tokens (counts as input)
- User prompt: 186 tokens (input)
- Model performs a function call; function name + arguments included in the request payload: 42 tokens (input)
- Model generates 387.4 tokens of text as the assistant response (tokenizers only return integer token counts in practice — round up conservatively): 388 tokens (output)
Billing calculation: input = 24 + 186 + 42 = 252 tokens; output = 388 tokens; total billed = 640 tokens for that API call.

Notes & edge cases:
- If you cache or prefix previously computed content via KV/prefix caching, you only pay when content is actually sent as part of the request/response payload.
- If a tool returns structured JSON that you never include in the assistant response (e.g., you persist it in your DB and don't echo it back), those tokens are not billed as output unless they are also included in a response body returned to the client.
- For multi-part requests (batching many prompts in one API call), we sum tokens across the batch and bill the aggregated total; there is no per-batch minimum beyond token granularity.
- Embedding calls are counted per embedding vector (different price unit). Retrieval connectors that stream documents to the model as part of the request are included in input token counts.

Pricing guidance for procurement (list vs commit):
- Public hosted list (example):
  * LLM-small: $0.002 / 1K input tokens, $0.006 / 1K output tokens
  * LLM-medium: $0.006 / 1K input tokens, $0.018 / 1K output tokens
  * LLM-large: $0.018 / 1K input tokens, $0.054 / 1K output tokens
- Typical committed discount bands (annual commit + term):
  * $250k annual commit: ~10% off list
  * $500k+ annual commit: ~15% - 20% off list (depending on term and billing cadence)
- We can also structure usage tiers with blended effective rates if Acme prefers predictable per-request pricing.

If you want, I can generate a short table with per-API example invoices for sample monthly volumes.

— Logan

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the forecast — attached is the current public rate card and a short, plain-English explanation from our product/pricing team (copied below). Max callouts:

• System tokens count as input. Function/tool arguments that you send as part of the request are input tokens. If the tool returns text and that text is included in the assistant response to your user, those tokens are counted as output (not double-counted).

• We meter per token (integer granularity). Streaming is billed as tokens are emitted; there are no hidden per-request minimums.

• Example (already prepared by Logan): input = system(24) + user(186) + function args(42) = 252 tokens; output = 388 tokens => total billed = 640 tokens.
